title: FIFO overflow queue (enqueue on limit, backpressure when full, drain as windows reset) — Epic 13
prompt:
Add a FIFO overflow queue with max depth from config: when a limit is hit, enqueue instead of dropping; signal backpressure when full; drain as rate windows reset.

Follow repo standards: TDD (write the failing test first, then code); max 150 lines per code file (split, don't compress); ruff = 0 violations + mypy clean; no hard-coded values (read from config); every external API call goes through the API gatekeeper (Epic 13); log via the LOG package; keep coverage >= 85%. Read docs/PRD.md and the relevant docs/prds/*.md before starting.

usage.summary: usage to be filled by main loop from harness report

note: Third task of Epic 13 (the API gatekeeper, docs/prds/api-gatekeeper.md §5): replaces 13.2's 'raise RateLimitExceededError on overflow' seam with the FIFO overflow queue — overflow is queued, never dropped or crashed. TDD red-first: wrote packages/core/tests/test_gatekeeper_queue.py first and watched it fail (ImportError: cannot import name 'QueueFullError'), then implemented. New module gatekeeper/_queue.py: _OverflowQueue (bounded collections.deque, max_depth from config, enqueue() returns False when full = backpressure, dequeue() FIFO) + PendingCall dataclass (captures deferred callable + args/kwargs) + lifetime enqueued_total/drained_total counters. execute() new contract: returns _T | None — runs the call immediately when the service window has room; if the per-minute/per-hour window is exhausted it ENQUEUES the call into the bounded per-service FIFO queue and returns None (runs later via drain()); only a genuinely FULL queue (depth == queue_max_depth) raises the new QueueFullError (backpressure signal). drain() walks each service's queue oldest-first, running calls while the limiter reports room (re-checks after each so a single freed slot releases exactly one call — FIFO preserved across window resets). The _RateLimiter clock is now injectable through the gatekeeper (ApiGatekeeper(..., time_fn=clock)) so a test advances the fake clock past the window then drains deterministically. Config: added a per-service queue_max_depth field (value 100) to config/rate_limits.json AND the ServiceLimits pydantic model (Field(gt=0)); the depth value lives ONLY in JSON — no depth literal in Python. Updated BOTH config shape tests for the additive field, keeping version '1.00' (additive, no bump): tests/test_rate_limits_config.py (0.14: REQUIRED_KEYS + EXPECTED_SERVICES) and packages/core/tests/test_rate_limit_config.py (13.1: field assertions + custom-payload fixtures). Rewrote the two 13.2 raise-on-overflow execute tests to assert ENQUEUE instead (test_rate_limit_checked_before_execution -> test_rate_limit_enqueues_instead_of_running; test_rate_limit_uses_config_values_not_hardcoded now asserts queue depth grows), and dropped the now-unused RateLimitExceededError import there. QueueStatus (types.py) is now REAL: get_queue_status(service) reports depth/max_depth/enqueued_total/drained_total from the live queue (full multi-service reporting is 13.5). Queue lifecycle events (enqueue/drain/backpressure) log via the LOG package (log_event, event_type='system', payload {service, queue_event}). RateLimitExceededError kept as an exported public type (the limiter's window-full signal) with a construction test. New QueueFullError exported from agent_debate.core.gatekeeper and agent_debate.core. 0 hard-coded values: queue depth + all limits come from config; only literals are identifier labels/unit conversions.
